questions.question: The __________ has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President** of India has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha.
 
• According to **Article 85** of the Constitution of India, the President can summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit.
 
• The President may from time to time prorogue the Houses or either House and dissolve the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• This power ensures that the President can manage the sessions of Parliament effectively, keeping in mind the legislative requirements and political climate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Prime Minister** advises the President regarding the summoning and proroguing of sessions of Parliament and the dissolution of Lok Sabha.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** heads the judiciary but does not have the power to summon or dissolve Parliament.
 
• The **Lok Sabha Speaker** presides over the sessions of the Lok Sabha but does not have the authority to summon or dissolve it.
 
• The role of the President in summoning and proroguing Parliament is a critical aspect of the functioning of the Indian parliamentary system, ensuring that legislative business is conducted smoothly.

questions.question: Who among the following is appointed as 25th Director General of Indian Coast Guard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rakesh Pal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rakesh Pal** has been appointed as the 25th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard.
 
• The Indian Coast Guard is a multi-mission organization, conducting round-the-year real-life operations at sea.
 
• Its roles include ensuring the safety and protection of artificial islands, offshore terminals, installations, and other structures.
 
• It also provides protection and assistance to fishermen and mariners at sea, and enforces maritime laws with respect to the country's maritime zones.
 
• The organization works in close cooperation with the Indian Navy, the Department of Fisheries, the Department of Revenue (Customs), and the Central and State police forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Coast Guard was formally established on **1 February 1977** by the Coast Guard Act, 1978 of the Parliament of India as an independent Armed force of India.
 
• The Indian Coast Guard's motto is **"Vayam Rakshamah" which means "We Protect"**.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Defence.
 
• The Indian Coast Guard has a diverse fleet of ships and aircraft to perform its duties effectively.
 
• Over the years, the Indian Coast Guard has made significant contributions to the safety and security of India's maritime zones.

questions.question: Who among the following people was popular as the "Nightingale of India"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarojini Naidu**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sarojini Naidu** was widely known as the "Nightingale of India".
 
• She was a celebrated poet and an Indian independence activist.
 
• Her work as a poet earned her the nickname "Nightingale of India" by Mahatma Gandhi because of the color, imagery, and lyrical quality of her poetry.
 
• She played a significant role in the Indian National Movement for independence from British rule.
 
• Sarojini Naidu was also the first woman to become the president of the Indian National Congress and the first woman to serve as a governor in independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sarojini Naidu was born on February 13, 1879, in Hyderabad, India.
 
• She was educated in Chennai, London, and Cambridge, and became involved in the Indian nationalist movement during the partition of Bengal in 1905.
 
• Her collection of poems, "The Golden Threshold", was published in 1905, and she went on to publish several other collections.
 
• Besides her literary work, she was also a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and participated in the Salt March, the Quit India Movement, and other significant campaigns.
 
• She passed away on March 2, 1949, but remains an enduring symbol of India's struggle for freedom and women's empowerment.

questions.question: Which game uses the Elo rating system to assess the skill levels of its players?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chess**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Elo rating system is primarily used in the game of **Chess** to assess the skill levels of its players.
 
• Developed by **Arpad Elo**, the system calculates the relative skill levels of players in two-player games such as chess.
 
• Many chess organizations, including the **FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs)**, use the Elo rating system to rank players.
 
• The system has been adapted for use in other games and sports, but it is most commonly associated with chess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Elo rating system was introduced in 1960 and has since become a standard in the chess world.
 
• A player's Elo rating is updated after each rated game based on the outcome and the ratings of the opponents.
 
• The system is designed to be self-correcting, meaning that a player's rating will stabilize around their true skill level over time.
 
• In addition to chess, the Elo rating system has been adapted for use in other sports and games, including **Go, Scrabble, and video games**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Fundamental Duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976 is related to the Fundamental Duties
The Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002 is related to the Fundamental Duties
Fundamental Duties are mentioned in PART VA in the Indian Constitution
Fundamental Duties are mentioned in Article 51A in the Indian Constitution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duties are mentioned in PART VA in the Indian Constitution**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976 is indeed related to the Fundamental Duties, as it introduced Article 51A which lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
 
• The Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002 added a new duty under Article 51A to provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 and 14 years.
 
• Fundamental Duties are mentioned in PART IV-A of the Indian Constitution, not PART VA. This makes option 3 incorrect.
 
• Fundamental Duties are indeed mentioned in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution to emphasize the obligation of the citizens towards the nation.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also be conscious of their duties towards the country.
 
• The inclusion of these duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union.
 
• Though not enforceable by law, the Fundamental Duties are considered vital for the holistic development of an individual's personality and the nation.

questions.question: With respect to the green revolution, what does 'HYV' stands for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Yielding Varieties**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **HYV** stands for **High Yielding Varieties**.
 
• These are varieties of crops that have been bred to produce more grain per plant compared to traditional varieties.
 
• HYV crops were a significant factor in the success of the Green Revolution, which aimed to increase food production in developing countries.
 
• Examples of HYV crops include certain strains of wheat, rice, and maize.
 
• The development and use of HYV crops have contributed to food security and agricultural productivity in many parts of the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** was initiated in the 1960s and aimed to increase food production through the use of modern agricultural techniques.
 
• It involved the use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation along with HYV seeds.
 
• The Green Revolution helped many countries, especially in Asia and Latin America, to achieve self-sufficiency in food production.
 
• However, it also brought challenges such as environmental degradation, increased inequality, and dependence on chemical inputs.
 
• Continuous research and development are necessary to improve HYV crops to address these challenges and ensure sustainable agricultural practices.

questions.question: Which element has the highest atomic number and is the heaviest naturally occurring element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uranium (U)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranium (U)** has the highest atomic number (92) among the naturally occurring elements.
 
• It is also **the heaviest naturally occurring element,** with a high atomic mass.
 
• **Uranium is primarily used as fuel in nuclear reactors **and in the production of nuclear weapons.
 
• Despite its heavy atomic mass, uranium can be found in various minerals such as uraninite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uranium was **discovered in 1789 **by German chemist **Martin Heinrich Klaproth**.
 
• It was **named after the planet Uranus**, which had been discovered eight years earlier.
 
• Uranium has several isotopes, i**ncluding Uranium-235 and Uranium-238**, which are used in different nuclear applications.
 
• Due to its radioactive properties, uranium must be handled with care to avoid potential health risks.
 
• Uranium is found in small amounts in rocks, soil, and water, and even in the human body in trace amounts.

questions.question: The aim of the MISTHI Scheme is to protect and revive ________ ecosystem on the Indian coast while enhancing the socio-economic status of nearby communities
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mangrove**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The aim of the **MISTHI Scheme** is to protect and revive the **mangrove** ecosystem on the Indian coast while enhancing the socio-economic status of nearby communities.
 
• Mangroves are crucial coastal ecosystems that provide numerous ecological services such as **coastal protection, habitat for marine life, and carbon sequestration**.
 
• Reviving mangrove ecosystems can help mitigate the effects of climate change and support the livelihoods of coastal communities through activities like fishing and tourism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mangroves act as natural barriers against storm surges and coastal erosion**, protecting inland areas from damage.
 
• They are also significant **for maintaining water quality by filtering pollutants and trapping sediments** from rivers and streams.
 
• The conservation and restoration of mangrove ecosystems are aligned with global environmental goals and commitments, such as **the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement**.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the dance form Chhau belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional dance form that originates from the state of **West Bengal**.
 
• It is also prevalent in the states of **Jharkhand** and **Odisha**.
 
• Chhau dance is recognized for its vigorous and energetic movements, often depicting themes from **Hindu epics** like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• The dance is performed during regional festivals, especially during the **Chaitra Parva**.
 
• Chhau dance has three distinct styles: **Purulia Chhau** (West Bengal), **Seraikella Chhau** (Jharkhand), and **Mayurbhanj Chhau** (Odisha).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chhau dance has been inscribed in the **UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in 2010.
 
• The dance typically involves the use of elaborate masks, which are crafted by skilled artisans.
 
• The themes of Chhau dance often revolve around the triumph of good over evil, reflecting deep-rooted cultural narratives.
 
• The music accompanying Chhau dance is played using traditional instruments like the **dhol**, **dhamsha**, and **shehnai**.
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve and promote this ancient art form through various cultural organizations and government initiatives.

questions.question: In south India, the _______ was a village assembly found in areas where the landowners were not brahmins.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ur**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ur** was a village assembly found in areas of South India where the landowners were not Brahmins.
 
• These assemblies played a crucial role in the local administration and management of village affairs.
 
• Ur assemblies were characterized by their inclusivity, allowing participation from various non-Brahmin landowning communities.
 
• They were responsible for various administrative functions including the management of resources, settling disputes, and organizing community activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chola Dynasty**, which ruled over South India from the 9th to 13th centuries, is particularly noted for its sophisticated administrative system, including the functioning of village assemblies like the **Ur**.
 
• These assemblies were often composed of elected members from the village, and their decisions were recorded in inscriptions on temple walls or stone slabs.
 
• Such local self-governing bodies were a significant feature of the Chola administration, reflecting the importance of local governance in ancient India.
 
• In addition to Ur, there were other types of assemblies such as **Sabhai** (for Brahmin villages) and **Nagaram** (for town assemblies), each serving different segments of society.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of green revolution in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M.S Swaminathan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M.S Swaminathan** is known as the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a period when agriculture in India was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technology such as high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers.
 
• Swaminathan is credited with playing a significant role in introducing and developing high-yielding varieties of wheat in India.
 
• His efforts helped India transform from a food-deficient nation to one of the world's leading agricultural nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sam Pitroda** is known for his contributions to the telecommunications sector in India.
 
• **Verghese Kurien** is known as the father of the White Revolution in India, which was responsible for making India the largest producer of milk in the world.
 
• **Durgesh Patel** does not have any notable contributions related to the Green Revolution.
 
• The Green Revolution began in the 1960s and was a significant turning point in Indian agriculture, leading to increased food grain production and self-sufficiency.
 
• Swaminathan has received several awards for his contributions, including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: Krishna Rao Shankar Pandit, Raja Bhaiya Poonchwale are associated with which Gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gwalior Gharana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishna Rao Shankar Pandit** and **Raja Bhaiya Poonchwale** are associated with the **Gwalior Gharana**.
 
• The Gwalior Gharana is one of the oldest and most prominent gharanas of Hindustani classical music.
 
• It has a rich history and is known for its khayal singing style.
 
• Krishna Rao Shankar Pandit and Raja Bhaiya Poonchwale were significant contributors to the propagation and development of this gharana.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gwalior Gharana is known for its simplicity and clarity in raga presentation.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of voice culture and systematic training.
 
• Other notable exponents of the Gwalior Gharana include Vishnu Digambar Paluskar and Balakrishnabuwa Ichalkaranjikar.
 
• The gharana has a significant influence on other gharanas and continues to be an essential part of Indian classical music.
